automated_checks.detail: hostname='claude' resolves=False. this node cannot resolve its own hostname 'claude' ([Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution). c10d rendezvous will hang indefinitely rather than fail. Fix: add '127.0.0.1 claude' to /etc/hosts, or launch with --rdzv-backend=static and an explicit --master-addr IP. Must be re-run ON EACH CLOUD NODE; a failure here hangs c10d rendezvous indefinitely rather than erroring (see reports/incidents/I-007).

cost_note: Budget alerts notify; they do not cap. The enforced caps are --max-run-duration with --instance-termination-action=DELETE per instance, train.max_steps and train.max_wall_seconds in the config, and running infra/gcp/teardown.sh unconditionally after every session.

manual_checks.question: Is the billing account upgraded from Free Trial to paid?
manual_checks.why: The Free Trial forbids attaching GPUs at all. Upgrading also enables charges beyond the remaining credit, which is why this is a human decision.

manual_checks.question: Is NVIDIA_L4_GPUS (or PREEMPTIBLE_NVIDIA_L4_GPUS) quota >= 2 in the target region?
manual_checks.why: New paid accounts start at 0. Quota requests take time and are sometimes denied.

manual_checks.question: Did a dry-run create succeed in the target zone?
manual_checks.why: Quota is permission, not inventory. Spot L4 capacity varies by zone and hour.

manual_checks.question: Is a budget alert set on the billing account?
manual_checks.why: Alerts NOTIFY, they do not CAP. Nothing in GCP stops spend automatically; the real cap is --max-run-duration on each instance plus teardown.

manual_checks.question: Is the credit expiry date recorded? (90 days from SIGNUP, not first use)
manual_checks.why: The clock starts at signup, so unused credit silently expires.

note: Manual items are recorded as UNANSWERED rather than defaulted to ok. A preflight that silently passes checks it cannot perform converts an unknown into a false assurance at exactly the moment money starts being spent.
